To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CD34+c-kit+CD38− subpopulation is the most primitive population of hematopoietic cells and has the highest proliferative potential, whereas the CD34+ c-kit+CD38+ subpopulation is the least primitive and has the lowest proliferative potential.
primitive progenitors of the hematopoietic system can be identified by the expression of CD34 and the lack of CD38 and/or c-kit.
the primitive stem/progenitors in human cord blood are enriched in CD38− and c-kit− cells and that telomerase expression correlates with the proliferative capacity of these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of primitive hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and their progenitors in human umbilical cord blood.
the characterization of the functional properties of CD34+ subpopulations in cord blood, which is a promising source of stem/progenitor hematopoietic cells for transplantation.
the identification of a population of stem cells that can be used in clinical applications, such as gene transfer and transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD34+c-kit+ and CD38+ cells are committed progenitor cells and CD34+c-kitsubset and CD38-subset cells are primitive stem cells, which can be used as the source of stem cells for transplantation.
the primitive hematopoietic stem cells are enriched in CD38− and c-kit− cells and that the CD34+c-kit-CD38- population is the most primitive stem cell.
CD34+ cells that are CD38- and c-kit- represent primitive hematopoietic stem cells that can generate LTC-IC and CFCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD34+ c-kit− CD38− cells are primitive stem/prognitor cells and that the telomerase activity of these cells is correlated with their proliferative potential and differentiation stage.
